question: Which part of the body acts as the rigid lever arm during movement?
explanation: Bones provide the rigid structure that functions as the lever arm in human body mechanics. [learn more](BMP112_U2_T3#BMP112_U2_T3_h1)

question: What part of the body serves as the fixed pivot point for a lever?
explanation: Joints act as the fulcrum, or fixed pivot point, around which skeletal lever arms rotate. [learn more](BMP112_U2_T3#BMP112_U2_T3_h1)

question: How are the parts arranged in a second-class lever?

options.A: Force is between two separate loads
options.B: Load is between the fulcrum and force
options.C: Force is between the fulcrum and load
options.D: Fulcrum is between the force and load

explanation: In a second-class lever, the load sits squarely between the pivot point and the muscular pull. [learn more](BMP112_U2_T3#BMP112_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which lever class has the fulcrum positioned right between the applied force and the load?
explanation: A first-class lever places the fulcrum right in the middle, resembling a traditional playground seesaw. [learn more](BMP112_U2_T3#BMP112_U2_T3_h2)

question: Which body movement shows a second-class lever system in action?

options.A: Nodding your head up and down
options.C: Bending your elbow to lift a cup

explanation: Standing on the toes places the load between the toe joints and the calf muscle force, creating a second-class lever. [learn more](BMP112_U2_T3#BMP112_U2_T3_h3)

question: What part of the body acts as the fulcrum when you nod your head up and down?
explanation: The skull pivots on the atlanto-occipital joint, forming a classic first-class lever setup in the upper spine. [learn more](BMP112_U2_T3#BMP112_U2_T3_h3)

question: Why is the third-class lever the most common in human limbs, even though it requires high muscular force?

options.A: It places the fulcrum at the very end of the limb
options.B: It provides great speed and a wide range of motion
options.C: It makes lifting heavy loads effortless
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for muscle energy

explanation: Third-class levers trade mechanical force for speed and distance, allowing fast and precise hand and foot movements. [learn more](BMP112_U2_T3#BMP112_U2_T3_h4)

question: Where is the applied muscular force located in a third-class lever?

options.B: Between the fulcrum and the load
options.D: At the far end away from the fulcrum

explanation: In third-class levers, the muscle insertion force acts in the middle space between the joint fulcrum and the terminal load. [learn more](BMP112_U2_T3#BMP112_U2_T3_h4)

question: What does a mechanical advantage of less than 1 mean for a skeletal lever?

options.A: It means the muscle force equals the load weight
options.B: It allows weak muscles to lift extremely heavy loads
options.C: It favors speed and range of motion over force
options.D: It stops movement from occurring at the joint

explanation: A mechanical advantage under 1 means the muscle must generate high force, but it gains speed and distance of movement. [learn more](BMP112_U2_T3#BMP112_U2_T3_h5)

question: How do you calculate mechanical advantage using lever arm lengths?

options.A: Force arm length divided by load arm length
options.B: Load arm length divided by force arm length
options.C: Load weight multiplied by the muscle length
options.D: Total bone length minus joint cavity width

explanation: Mechanical advantage is found by dividing the distance from the fulcrum to the applied force by the distance from the fulcrum to the load. [learn more](BMP112_U2_T3#BMP112_U2_T3_h5)

question: Why does lifting a heavy object with a rounded back put high stress on back muscles?

options.A: It eliminates the fulcrum entirely from the vertebral column
options.B: It creates a long load arm that requires huge muscle force
options.C: It reduces the mechanical advantage to a value above 5.0
options.D: It turns the spine into a highly efficient second-class lever

explanation: Bending forward increases the distance of the load from the spinal fulcrum, forcing back muscles to exert massive tension. [learn more](BMP112_U2_T3#BMP112_U2_T3_h6)

question: Which of these is NOT a safe practice when lifting heavy objects to protect your spine?

options.A: Using leg muscles rather than back muscles to lift
options.B: Keeping the heavy load close to the center of the body
options.C: Bending primarily from the waist with straight knees
options.D: Keeping your feet apart to widen the base of support

explanation: Bending from the waist increases spinal leverage stress; safe lifting requires bending the knees and hips instead. [learn more](BMP112_U2_T3#BMP112_U2_T3_h6)
